gloss: to stand out; to be set off; to look more attractive (by contrast or context)

definitions.gloss: to stand out; to be set off; to look more attractive (by contrast or context)
definitions.explanation: to stand out; to be set off; to look more attractive (by contrast or context)

examples.japanese: {白|しろ}い{皿|さら}で{料理|りょうり}の{色|いろ}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}つ。
examples.english: The colors of the food stand out on a white plate.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}いドレスが{彼女|かのじょ}の{美|うつく}しさを{引|ひ}き{立|た}てている。
examples.english: The red dress sets off her beauty.

examples.japanese: シンプルな{額縁|がくぶち}のおかげで、{絵|え}そのものの{魅力|みりょく}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}っている。
examples.english: Thanks to the simple frame, the appeal of the painting itself stands out.

examples.japanese: わさびを{少|すこ}し{加|くわ}えると、{刺身|さしみ}の{味|あじ}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}つ。
examples.english: Adding a little wasabi brings out the flavor of the sashimi.

notes:
Describes something looking more attractive, prominent, or noticeable thanks to its context, contrast, or an accompanying element. Used for visual appearance, flavors, talents, and other qualities. The transitive counterpart is {引|ひ}き{立|た}てる (to set off; to make something stand out).

TRANSITIVITY:
- {引|ひ}き{立|た}つ (intransitive): to stand out
- {引|ひ}き{立|た}てる (transitive): to make something stand out; to set off; to promote

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色|いろ}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}つ: colors stand out
- {味|あじ}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}つ: flavor is brought out
- {魅力|みりょく}が{引|ひ}き{立|た}つ: charm stands out
- お{互|たが}いを{引|ひ}き{立|た}てる: to bring out the best in each other

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {目立|めだ}つ: to stand out; to be conspicuous — can be positive or negative, while {引|ひ}き{立|た}つ always implies looking better or more attractive
- {映|は}える: to look good; to be photogenic — focuses on visual appeal, especially in photography or against a background
